paragraphs: Roofers first inspect the substrate, slope, old roof, and leak points, then lay shingles, membrane, or metal roofing per drawings and material instructions, handling seams, waterproofing, and edge details; they stop work and escalate when fall protection, weather, or ignition-source conditions are unclear.

Carpenters handle wood structures and substrates, sheet metal workers fabricate metal panels, waterproofers can handle waterproofing in many parts of a building, and solar photovoltaic installers fasten modules. Roofers are responsible for roof covering, waterproofing details, leak checking, and repair, and related work requires verifying the division of duties.

AI can help organize survey photos, material lists, and leak-check records, but cannot independently confirm substrate load capacity, roof leaks, bonding quality, wind and rain conditions, or fall protection; on-site acceptance is the responsibility of trained personnel.

This page is based on O*NET tasks and fictional roofing practice and does not predict individual hiring; work at height, hot application, electrical, or structural changes must be verified per location and employer procedures.

The BLS 2025 median annual wage for U.S. roofers is 55,440 U.S. dollars; 2025—2035 employment rises from about 166,900 to 175,600, a growth of 5.3%, with about 12,000 annual openings. Chinese construction wages serve only as industry background.

Roofers (O*NET 47-2181.00) inspect problem roofs, prepare substrates, cut and lay covering materials such as shingles, membrane, and metal panels, handle waterproofing, drainage, and edge details, and perform leak checks and repairs. Fall protection, hot application, and roof structure changes follow special plans.

O*NET 47-2181.00 provides roofer tasks and work activities; the BLS 2025—2035 occupational projections table for 47-2181 gives employment and median annual wages, and the O*NET national wage page gives BLS 2025 percentiles. The survey scope, period, and occupational codes of different statistical programs must be labeled separately.
